correctness.rationale: Cauchy's formula assigns each facet a centered segment with half-vector A_F n_F/2; an antipodal pair combines to one segment with half-vector A_F n_F. The three-dimensional zonotope volume is eight times the absolute triple-determinant sum in these half-vector conventions. An exact independent reconstruction, python3 /workspace/branches/check_platonic.py, starts with the frozen original vertices, enumerates supporting triples and recovers all facets, orders their boundaries, computes outward area vectors and body volumes, and sums all determinant contributions. All signs are computed in Q(sqrt(5)) without floating point. It verifies the five facets counts 6,20,12,8,4 in the order displayed, both antipodal determinant spectra, the golden-body projection volumes 1120+640sqrt(5) and 800sqrt(5), and all five ratios. The strict comparisons reduce to 5·63²>139², 5·12²>26² and 34²>5·15² between positive quantities, followed by 9<18. For example the squared equal-volume circumradius comparison gives (R(I)^3/vol(I))^2−(R(D)^3/vol(D))^2=9(sqrt(5)−2)/80>0, opposite to the ratio order. Affine covariance Π(TK)=|det T|T^(−t)Π(K) is consistent with the squared volume normalization in dimension three. No general projection-volume inequality is being verified.

evidence: The Equilateral Zonohedron basis table assigns 10 dodecahedral diameters to the rhombic enneacontahedron and 6 icosahedral diameters to the rhombic triacontahedron.

A Platonic solid has equal area facets and facet-normal directions given by the vertices of its dual. For the centrally symmetric pair the half-vectors are A_F n_F, precisely the equilateral generators of those two named zonohedra.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The generators identify the entire Minkowski sum up to a single scaling and rigid motion, not just a similar-looking polyhedron. The full length of a generator equals an edge length: expose its segment by a vector orthogonal only to that generator, so the others give endpoints. Thus edge a is 2sqrt(3) for ΠI and 2A_D for ΠD.

Rhombic Triacontahedron Eq. (8): volume 4sqrt(5+2sqrt(5)) a³. McCooey's metrics list the same solid with edge sqrt(10(5+sqrt(5)))/8 and volume 25(5+2sqrt(5))/16 in the dual unit-edge icosidodecahedron normalization, giving the same coefficient on dividing by the edge cubed.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are exact tables of the numerators in an edge normalization, not of a different shadow invariant. Their applicability is determined by the generator identifications. A separate exact table of the ratios is unnecessary for coverage.

originality.rationale: Both advertised new numbers are mechanically implied by existing volume tables under equivalent zonohedron names. The projection body of the icosahedron is the rhombic enneacontahedron scaled to edge 2sqrt(3), and that of the dodecahedron is the rhombic triacontahedron scaled to edge 2A_D. The basis-direction table and the exact volume formulas were independently inspected. These imply both volumes, ratios and the complete ordering with existing benchmarks. This establishes scientific coverage irrespective of whether a source lists the ratios in this notation or explicitly sorts them.
residual_risks: The comparison establishes coverage under known equivalent shape names, not a date or claim about who first expressed these exact quotients in projection-body notation.
The additional cited article sections and same-date catalogue full text were not all available. Those gaps do not change the exact implication of the directly inspected basis and volume tables.

value.rationale: P is a natural affine-invariant benchmark and the five-body comparison is correct, but the frozen claim limits its increment to the two computed ratios and their ranking. They are recoverable by routine normalization and arithmetic from the exact existing tables once the dual normal sets are identified. The minor tables are auxiliary certificates for those evaluations, not an independently motivated surviving theorem in the frozen record. This is a rejection of the proposed incremental result, not of the usefulness of the invariant.
